title: Hardware wallet manufacturers report surge in demand
content:
TL;DR: Hardware wallet manufacturers are reporting a significant surge in demand, signaling a global shift towards self-custody as individuals increasingly seek monetary sovereignty. This move underscores a growing understanding that true ownership of Bitcoin means holding your own keys, secured by the network's formidable 911.90 EH/s hashrate, which defends against censorship and confiscation. For transactors, this means re-evaluating personal security practices and preparing for a future where taking custody is paramount.

The Report

February 05, 2026, 12:30 UTC – In a development signaling a profound shift in how individuals interact with their digital assets, leading hardware wallet manufacturers are reporting an unprecedented surge in demand. Companies like Ledger, Trezor, and Coldcard have confirmed a significant uptick in orders, with some reporting backlogs stretching weeks, indicating a widespread movement towards self-custody among Bitcoin holders globally. This trend is not merely anecdotal; it reflects a growing awareness of the fundamental principle of "not your keys, not your Bitcoin," driven by a complex interplay of geopolitical instability, economic uncertainty, and a maturing understanding of digital bearer assets.
